name: Kɪtʊlɛ / Yi Kitule
catalog_citation: Blench, Roger. 2020. The phonology and noun morphology of Yi Kitʊlɛ, an Adamawa language of East-Central Nigeria. Language in Africa 1(3): 155-180. doi:10.37892/2686-8946-2020-1-3-155-180. Author-site offprint PDF (rogerblench.info) via Wayback 20240612.
catalog_quote: There are three level tones plus rising and falling glides. ... 2.3. Tones Kɪtʊlɛ has three level tones, and glide tones that arise from sequences of level tones. ... It is assumed in this paper that the basic tone-bearing unit (TBU) is a single vowel, and that bimoraic sequences of two similar vowels can therefore bear either similar or dissimilar tones. Some examples of minimal triplets illustrating the three tone-heights: fúr 'grave' ~ fur 'to bury' ~ fùr 'stomach' ... Contour tones are rare and unpredictable but in all cases the syllable coda is a sonorant. ... Melodies at the word level are very diverse and only a few observations can be entered here. Tone melodies on disyllabic words exhibit all possible combinations, as shown in Table 8. ... Trisyllabic roots, which are predominantly nominals, have a strong tendency to exhibit LLL tone patterns as in Table 9. ... This may reflect…

audit.reasoning: (1) The deciding quotation is verbatim in the held Blench 2020 offprint at the stated places (abstract p.155; sec. 2.3 pp.164-165), and the paper contains no stress/accent/prominence statement, so kind=tonal (TONAL-OR-PITCH-ACCENT), domain UNSTATED, rule fields empty are faithful to the source. (2) The source is a 2020 peer-reviewed phonology article by a fieldworker, the most recent and only tone-aware description of the language; the alternatives in Glottolog are a 1955/56 write-up of anonymous missionary notes (which Blench says omits tone) and a 2-page 1925 mission note. (3) Nothing open and unheld would change the coding; the Mainz wordlist was fetched sources and is silent.
